title: SPD instrument — luminance-weighted plane dominance, baseline red printed
summary: HERO-FOLD-v2 §3 turns 'the plane dominates' into a number. Author scripts/validate/hero_plane_dominance.mjs and tests/overhaul/hero-plane-dominance.spec.ts. Capture the fold at dsf 1; L = WCAG relative luminance (reuse the helper in tests/overhaul/flagship-visibility.spec.ts); ground G = 10th-percentile L of the fold; light mass m = max(0, L - G). Ink set I = union of fold text-leaf rects + media rects (img/video/svg) + every element whose computed background-color alpha >= 0.5, each dilated 8px, read from the live DOM. Plane P = fold minus I. TC-HERO-PLANE-01 asserts SPD = sum_P(m)/sum_fold(m) >= 0.75; TC-HERO-PLANE-02 asserts the PLANE-2 floor sum_fold(m)/(W*H) >= 0.045 so a black fold cannot score 1.0. Run at 1440x900, 1280x800, 834x1194, 390x844 on BOTH /?gl=force and the reduced-motion still. Print G, sum_fold m, sum_P m, SPD and the excluded rect list in every assertion message so a reviewer re-derives rather than trusts. Record the red baseline; change no production file. Runs in parallel with g2h1-02 — this lane is the gate, that lane is the first visible pixel.
order: Read tests/overhaul/flagship-visibility.spec.ts for the luminance helper, the isolated-slot capture and the ?gl=force + settle pattern
Read tests/e2e/hero-fold.spec.ts for FOLD/STAGE/PORTRAIT_IMG selectors and the foldArea helper
Author scripts/validate/hero_plane_dominance.mjs as the shared measurement (importable by the spec, runnable standalone with --base)
Author tests/overhaul/hero-plane-dominance.spec.ts with TC-HERO-PLANE-01 and TC-HERO-PLANE-02 parameterised over 4 widths x 2 paths
Capture the baseline: docs/delivery/evidence/v10-20260905T0515Z/G2H1/01/02-tests-failing.log with the real SPD per width per path
Confirm the DOM rect exclusion list is printed, not summarised — a reviewer must be able to reproduce I
gates: Thresholds are exactly 0.75 (SPD) and 0.045 (PLANE-2); lowering either to make a run green is a violation
Ground G is measured from the capture, never assumed from a declared background-color
Both paths measured — a GPU-only number is not evidence for the no-GL reader
Zero production files touched; git diff --name-only shows only scripts/validate, tests/ and docs/delivery/evidence

title: M1 — the light reaches the left: retire the desktop half-frame scrim for per-run plates
summary: HERO-FOLD-v2 §2 M1 / decision D-1. Hero.module.css .stage::after paints rgb(10 10 10 / 0.88) from 0% to 44% and 0.86->0.45 out to 56% — the half of the frame the eye enters through is switched off, which is the whole of 'cinematic stage reads as wallpaper'. Delete that wash above 700px and buy the contrast locally instead: promote the phone instrument (@media (max-width: 700px): background rgb(10 10 10 / 0.90), border-radius 3px, padding-inline .45rem, margin-inline -.45rem on .eyebrow/.name/.role/.statement plus the secondary action) to every width, sized to each run's own box and not a pixel wider. The 0.90 alpha is measured, not chosen: over this shader's brightest fog (0.8308 relative luminance) it lands the ground on #212121, inside the #2A2A2A ceiling --mist-400 needs for 4.5:1. Do NOT remove the <=700px rule — this extends it upward. VISIBLE: the atmosphere appears behind the copy at 1440/1280 where today it is 88% black. This is the first visible slice of the lane.

title: M2 — the name becomes a mark: one line, full measure, display tracking
summary: HERO-FOLD-v2 §4 / decision D-2, D-6. 'Vikram Deshpande' wraps to two lines today: --fs-name is clamp(3rem, 8.2vw, 7.5rem) = 118px at 1440 inside a ~660px column (h1 top 183, .role top 453 on live e3f0206c). A wrapped name is a heading; a single line set to the measure is a mark. Collapse the @media (min-width: 720px) two-column grid so the copy takes the full --page-max measure, then DERIVE --fs-name from a real browser measurement of the text advance — do not ship the brief's 166px/11.5vw arithmetic, it is an estimate with a stated metric assumption. Acceptance BM-1 (h1 height <= 1.30x font-size at 1440/1280/834), BM-2 (advance 0.86-1.00 of the column), BM-3 (font-size >= 0.10 x fold height), BM-4 (letter-spacing -0.035em..-0.015em), BM-6 (no other fold node > 40px), BM-7 (scrollWidth <= innerWidth), BM-8 (>= 6x the nav wordmark cap-height). At 390 ship BM-1b instead: exactly two line boxes from an authored break, leading <= 0.92em. .name keeps heroRiseSolid — transform only, never opacity — or the LCP entry disappears.

title: M3 — the photograph loses its card: drafting frame out, edges masked into the light
summary: HERO-FOLD-v2 §5.1 / decision D-3. HeroPortrait.tsx draws .portraitFrame (a hairline inset 12px), four .portraitTick corners and .portraitCross — a closed rectangle with registration marks parked in a second column, which is exactly what the 1451Z reviewer called 'a framed card beside a column'. Remove those three from the FOLD only (the drafting language stays on the caliper mark and in the proof band) and apply a composite mask-image to .portraitMedia so the outer edges fall off into the plane. Place the figure overlapping the mark's right end rather than beside it. Acceptance PH-1 (no border/outline/box-shadow on the media box or its children; zero portrait-tick nodes in the fold), PH-2 (mean |dL| across the rect boundary <= 0.04 on >= 3 of 4 edges, sampled 4px in vs 4px out), PH-3 (mask opaque over the upper-centre 46% — no gradient crosses the face), PH-4 (still a <figure> with a <figcaption>, figurePressables === 0), PH-5 (CLS 0 — a mask is compositing, no box resizes). Colour-agnostic by construction: nothing here samples inside the media rect, so the t_g2_h6 decision changes one filter declaration and nothing else.

title: M4 — the pool comes to the figure: bind poolPlate to the portrait, re-render the poster
summary: HERO-FOLD-v2 §5.2 / decision D-7. atmosphere.glsl.ts already writes the pool for this — 'vec2 q2 = (p - vec2(0.75 * halfWidth, -0.04) ...)', whose own comment says it stands behind the portrait plate — but the pool is a constant and the figure is a layout, so after g2h1-04 they no longer coincide. Add a uPortrait uniform (normalised centre, defaulting to today's constant so the shader is byte-equivalent until it is fed), set it from the figure's measured rect in HeroAtmosphere.tsx, and mirror the same centre in .stage's radial fallback so the no-GL reader gets the same picture. Then re-run node scripts/assets/render-hero-poster.mjs IN THE SAME COMMIT: the poster is rendered from this shader, so a shader change without a re-render silently desynchronises the first-paint path. Acceptance PL-1 (of the fold's brightest 5% of pixels, >= 60% lie within 1.3x the media rect's half-diagonal of its centre, ?gl=force at 1440), PL-2 (same on the reduced-motion still, >= 50%), PL-3 (the commit touches both the shader and the poster), PL-4 (poster <= 500 kB, 3840x2160).

title: The CTA group as one quiet bar — one row, one plate, contrast kept, area cut
